China is the [world's most populous country](List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"), and its largest city, <Shanghai>, is the largest city proper in the world, with a population of 26.3 million as of 2019.[[1]](List_of_cities_in_China_by_population#cite_note-1) According to the Demographia research group, in 2017, there were 102 Chinese cities with over 1 million people in the "urban area", as defined by the group's methodology.[[2]](List_of_cities_in_China_by_population#cite_note-demographia-2)

## Definition and classification

According to the [administrative divisions of China](Administrative_divisions_of_China "Administrative divisions of China"), there are three levels of cities, namely [direct-administered municipalities](Direct-administered_municipalities_of_China "Direct-administered municipalities of China") (直辖市), [prefecture-level cities](Prefecture-level_city "Prefecture-level city") (地级市), and [county-level cities](County-level_city "County-level city") (县级市). The [special administrative regions](Special_administrative_regions_of_China "Special administrative regions of China") (特别行政区) of [Hong Kong](Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and <Macau> are not included in this administrative classification.

Municipalities and prefecture-level cities are not each a 'city' in the strictest sense of the term, but are, instead, an administrative unit comprising, typically, both the [urban core](Urban_area "Urban area") (*a city in the strict sense*) and surrounding [rural](Rural_area "Rural area") or less-urbanized areas.[[3]](List_of_cities_in_China_by_population#cite_note-3)

Prefecture-level cities nearly always contain multiple [counties](Counties_of_China "Counties of China") (县), [county-level cities](County-level_city "County-level city"), and other such sub-divisions. To distinguish a prefecture-level city from its actual urban area (*city in the strict sense*), the term "市区" (*shì qū*; "urban area") is used. However, even this term often encompasses large suburban regions often greater than 3,000 square kilometres (1,000 sq mi), sometimes only the urban core, whereas the agglomeration overtakes the city limits. Thus, the "urban core" would be roughly comparable to the American term "city limit", the "shì qū", or "urban area", would be roughly comparable to "metropolitan area", and the municipality is a political designation defining regions under control of a municipal government, which has no comparable designation.

While in 2013 <Chongqing> had the largest population total of any special municipality, 28 million, only 4.5 million of the people were in the actual Chongqing urban area, with the remainder of the population in suburban and rural areas.[[4]](List_of_cities_in_China_by_population#cite_note-4)

## List of major cities by population

The vast majority of Shanghai's land area is flat, apart from a few hills in the southwest corner, due to its location on the [alluvial plain](Alluvial_plain "Alluvial plain") of the Yangtze's river delta. The city has many [rivers](River "River") and [lakes](Lake "Lake") and is known for its rich water resources, and thanks to its coastal, riverside location and warm climate ensuring ice-free waters, provides easy access to China's interior, resulting in Shanghai being the world's largest [port](Port "Port").[[1]](Geography_of_Shanghai#cite_note-largestport-1)
